classification.difficultyReason: The apex is above a base-edge midpoint, requiring different perpendicular heights for the triangular faces before their areas are added.

content.prompt:
In the pyramid below, $F$ is the midpoint of $AB$. $VF$ is vertical and is $5\text{ m}$ in length. $ABCD$ is horizontal and rectangular, with $AB=6\text{ m}$ and $BC=8\text{ m}$.

Find:

spec.description: Rectangular-based pyramid with apex vertically above F, the midpoint of rear edge AB. Visible edges VD, VC, VB, DC and CB are solid; hidden edges DA, AB and AV are dashed. The altitude VF is red dashed and has a right-angle marker at F. No face fills.
spec.mathematics: AB=6 m, BC=8 m, AF=FB=3 m and VF=5 m. F lies on AB, not at the centre of the rectangle.
spec.answerVisibility: Only source labels and structural givens are visible; no calculated lengths or answers.

children.label: b
children.prompt: the surface area of this solid

inlines.text: Use Pythagoras’ theorem to find the face heights, then add the four triangular faces and the rectangular base.

answer.worked:
$$\begin{align*}AF=FB&=\frac62=3\text{ m}\\VA^2=VB^2&=5^2+3^2=34\\VA=VB&=\sqrt{34}\text{ m}\end{align*}$$
Since $AD$ and $BC$ are perpendicular to the vertical plane $VAB$, $VA$ and $VB$ are the perpendicular heights of faces $VAD$ and $VBC$.
$$\begin{align*}A_{VAD}+A_{VBC}&=2\times\frac12\times8\times\sqrt{34}\\A_{VAD}+A_{VBC}&=8\sqrt{34}\text{ m}^2\\A_{VAB}&=\frac12\times6\times5\\A_{VAB}&=15\text{ m}^2\end{align*}$$
Let $M$ be the midpoint of $DC$. Then $FM=8\text{ m}$ and $VM$ is the perpendicular height of face $VDC$.
$$\begin{align*}VM^2&=5^2+8^2=89\\VM&=\sqrt{89}\text{ m}\\A_{VDC}&=\frac12\times6\times\sqrt{89}\\A_{VDC}&=3\sqrt{89}\text{ m}^2\\A_{\text{base}}&=6\times8=48\text{ m}^2\\S&=48+15+8\sqrt{34}+3\sqrt{89}\\S&=(63+8\sqrt{34}+3\sqrt{89})\text{ m}^2\end{align*}$$
